arxiv-2104-02480.title: Pickers’ Guide to Acoustics of the Banjo, parts I and II
arxiv-2104-02480.creator: David Politzer ∗ , Jim Woodhouse † , and Hossein Mansour +
arxiv-2104-02480.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by David Politzer ∗ , Jim Woodhouse † , and Hossein Mansour +. The results of an investigation of fundamental banjo acoustics and physics are now readily available. The papers describe measurements and calculations which demonstrate the extent to which the sound of a banjo can be represented by linear modeling of the basic parts common to the banjo family: strings, drum head, light floating bridge, and break angle. This note summarizes the conclusions of that work and outlines some of the physics involved.

arxiv-2106-12560.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. Kumar, H. D. Singh, A. K. Prasad. In this paper, we study the stellar structure in terms of alternative theory of gravity specially by f ⁡ ( R , T ) f(R,T) gravity theory. Here, we consider the function f ⁡ ( R , T ) = R + 2 ​ ς ​ T f(R,T)=R+2\varsigma T where R R is the Ricci scalar, T T is the stress-energy momentum and ς \varsigma is the coupling constant.

arxiv-2108-02549.title: Ultrastrong capacitive coupling of flux qubits
arxiv-2108-02549.creator: Mar\́mathrm{i}a Hita-Pérez, Gabriel Jaumà, Manuel Pino, Juan José Garc\́mathrm{i}a-Ripoll
arxiv-2108-02549.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mar\́mathrm{i}a Hita-Pérez, Gabriel Jaumà, Manuel Pino, Juan José Garc\́mathrm{i}a-Ripoll. A flux qubit can interact strongly when it is capacitively coupled to other circuit elements. This interaction can be separated in two parts, one acting on the qubit subspaces and one in which excited states mediate the interaction.

arxiv-2204-02649.creator: Hua-Xing Chen, Wei Chen, Xiang Liu, Yan-Rui Liu and Shi-Lin Zhu
arxiv-2204-02649.description: Abstract The past decades witnessed the golden era of hadron physics. Many excited open heavy flavor mesons and baryons have been observed since 2017. We shall provide an updated review of the recent experimental and theoretical progresses in this active field.

arxiv-2304-03221.title: Degrees of interior polynomials and parking function enumerators
arxiv-2304-03221.creator: Tamás Kálmán, Lilla Tóthmérész
arxiv-2304-03221.description: Abstract . The interior polynomial of a directed graph is defined as the h ∗ h^{*} -polynomial of the graph’s (extended) root polytope, and it displays several attractive properties. Here we express its degree in terms of the minimum cardinality of a directed join, and give a formula for the leading coefficient.

arxiv-2305-10659.title: Use of Speech Impairment Severity for Dysarthric Speech Recognition
arxiv-2305-10659.creator: Mengzhe Geng, Zengrui Jin, Tianzi Wang, Shujie Hu, Jiajun Deng, Mingyu Cui, Guinan Li, Jianwei Yu, Xurong Xie, Xunying Liu

A key challenge in dysarthric speech recognition is the speaker-level diversity attributed to both speaker-identity associated factors such as gender, and speech impairment severity. Most prior researches on addressing this issue focused on using speaker-identity only.

arxiv-2310-07639.title: Guidance of ultraviolet light down to 190 nm in a hollow-core optical fibre Journal: opticajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2310-07639.creator: Robbie Mears, 1,* Kerrianne Harrington, 1 William J. Wadsworth, 1 Jonathan C Knight, 1 James M Stone, 1 Tim A Birks, 1
arxiv-2310-07639.description: Abstract We report an anti-resonant hollow core fibre with ultraviolet transmission down to 190 nm, covering the entire UV-A, UV-B and much of the UV-C band. Guidance from 190 - 400 nm is achieved apart for a narrow high loss resonance band at 245 – 265 nm. The minimum attenuation is 0.13 dB/m at 235 nm and 0.

arxiv-2408-12000.title: Gevrey Regularity for a Fluid-Structure Interaction Model Thanks: Author 1 partially supported by NSF Grant DMS-1948942
arxiv-2408-12000.creator: George Avalos, Dylan McKnight, Sara McKnight
arxiv-2408-12000.description: Abstract . A result of Gevrey regularity is ascertained for a semigroup which models a fluid-structure interaction problem. In this model, the fluid evolves in a piecewise smooth or convex geometry 𝒪 \mathcal{O} . On a portion of the boundary, a fourth order plate equation is coupled with the fluid through pressure and matching velocities.

pmc-11382210.creator: Riccardo Leni, Emily A. Vertosick, Roderick C.N. van den Bergh, Timo F.W. Soeterik, Joris G. Heetman, Harm H.E. van Melick, Marco Roscigno, Giovanni La Croce, Luigi F. Da Pozzo, Jonathan Olivier, Fabio Zattoni, Matteo Facco, Fabrizio Dal Moro, Peter K.F. Chiu, Xiaobo Wu, Isabel Heidegger, Giulia Gia
pmc-11382210.description: Take Home MessageWe analyzed the long-term outcomes of patients with grade group (GG) 1 prostate cancer on active surveillance according to whether their initial diagnosis was on biopsy or incidental following a procedure to relieve urinary symptoms. Patients with incidental prostate cancer had a lower incidence of metastases and transition to treatment than patients diagnosed on biopsies.

pmc-11532369.title: Multimodal AI/ML for discovering novel biomarkers and predicting disease using multi-omics profiles of patients with cardiovascular diseases
pmc-11532369.creator: William DeGroat, Habiba Abdelhalim, Elizabeth Peker, Neev Sheth, Rishabh Narayanan, Saman Zeeshan, Bruce T Liang, Zeeshan Ahmed
pmc-11532369.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are complex, multifactorial conditions that require personalized assessment and treatment. Advancements in multi-omics technologies, namely RNA sequencing and whole-genome sequencing, have provided translational researchers with a comprehensive view of the human genome. The efficient synthesis and analysis of this data through integrated approach that characterizes genetic variants alongside expression patterns linked to emerging phenotypes, can reveal novel biomarkers and enable the segmentation of patient populations based on personalized risk factors.

pmc-12562297.description: As the core refrigeration equipment in cooling systems, the operational state of chiller units is crucial for ship support, equipment cooling, and mission stability. pmc-13448444.title: Integrative transcriptomics and single-cell analysis identify SIX4 as a candidate epithelial target in ovarian cancer and PCOS-associated ovarian dysregulation
pmc-13448444.creator: Xuan Li, Gaowen Chen, Yifeng Wang, Chunfang Ha
pmc-13448444.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights•Single-cell-guided transcriptomics prioritized SIX4 in ovarian cancer.•SIX4 was enriched in tumor epithelial compartments of ovarian cancer.•PCOS-associated ovarian dysregulation provided a comorbidity context.•SIX4 knockdown suppressed SKOV3 proliferation, migration and colony growth.•Docking and MD suggested a testable SIX4-centered therapeutic axis.Keywords: Ovarian cancer, Polycystic ovary syndrome, Single-cell RNA sequencing, Machine learning, Biomarker prioritization

Introduction

Ovarian cancer is a highly lethal gynecologic solid tumor characterized by late-stage diagnosis, frequent therapeutic resistance, and marked molecular heterogeneity [1,2].

pmc-13575102.title: A novel multiomics machine learning signature identifies rapid progression in clinically low risk prostate cancer
pmc-13575102.creator: Alexandra Rafeletou, Faezeh Fathi, Tatjana Kiseļova, Golnaz Taheri, Arian Lundberg
pmc-13575102.description: Risk stratification in primary prostate cancer remains heavily reliant on clinicopathological criteria that frequently miss the heterogeneity underlying early aggressive disease. We present a novel machine learning non-linear prognostic framework encoding somatic copy-number alterations and biological information associated with gene products, along with an integrative multi-omics approach including epigenomics and transcriptomics into a patient-specific biological network.
